links.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM mortality risk estimates across two repeated runs (Bland-Altman bias)
links.effect: Mean difference between repeats was 1.28% (95% CI 0.09-2.47) for GPT-4o and 0.18% (95% CI -0.41-0.76) for GPT-5, so GPT-4o showed a small systematic run-to-run difference and GPT-5 did not.
links.quote: Agreement analysis showed a mean difference (bias) of 1.28% (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.09-2.47) for GPT-4o and 0.18% (95% CI, -0.41-0.76) for GPT-5.

screen.reason: Retrospective study evaluating the performance and reproducibility of multimodal LLMs (GPT-4o and a speculative GPT-5 prompt setup) to predict post-operative mortality from patient records and images without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
